message.content:
In blackjack, **an Ace is worth either 1 or 11**—whichever gives your hand the best possible score without going over 21.  

* If counting the Ace as 11 keeps the total ≤ 21, it’s treated as 11 (“soft” hand).  
* If adding 11 would cause a bust, the Ace automatically becomes 1 (“hard” hand).

This dual‑value feature lets players keep their options open until they’re forced to decide when drawing more cards. Casinos sometimes phrase this differently (e.g., “the dealer will hit on a soft 17”), but the underlying rule remains the same: choose the Ace’s value that maximizes your hand while staying under 22.
